newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oil price, dollar drive Norwegian stocks higher.
newsitem.headline: Oil price, dollar drive Norwegian stocks higher.

text.p: Norwegian share prices advanced on Thursday to reverse day-earlier losses, driven up by a firm dollar and a further jump in oil prices on rising Middle East tensions.
The Total share index climbed more than five points to 836.74 points, a gain of 0.61 percent, in moderate turnover of 515 million crowns.
Brokers said, however, investors remained cautious in the see-saw market, which would remain reliant on the United States for direction.

Oil-sensitive stocks Norsk Hydro and Saga Petroleum benefitted from the latest tusseling between Iraq and the United States. Prices for benchmark Brent crude reached new five-year highs at $24.39 per barrel on speculation of U.S. attacks on Iraq in retaliation of Iraqi attacks on U.S. warplanes.
Hydro closed four crowns up at 303.50 crowns while Saga A gained one crown at 106 crowns.

UNI Storebrand rose one crown to 36.70 crowns on a positive outlook report from investment bank Goldman Sachs. Goldman rated UNI as a market outperformer and forecast its stock price to rise by about 30 percent in the next 16 months.
